description: The first aeroplane built in Ethiopia. Designed by Wilhelm von Nes from his earlier A.VII and constructed in Addis Ababa during 1935 by the German engineer Ludwig Weber with Junkers mechanics welding the steel-tube fuselage and a German glider specialist building the wooden wings. Two-seat dual-control fabric-covered monoplane with a seven-cylinder Walter Venus I of 115 hp and a Schwartz wooden propeller. First flight December 1935. Abandoned at Jan Meda in May 1936, seized by Italian forces and held at the Vigna di Valle aviation museum until the Italian government returned it in February 2024 during Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's visit to Rome. Ethiopian Monitor reported it was transferred to the Adwa Victory Memorial Museum on arrival. No registration was ever carried; the fuselage bore the Amharic name only.
